description: Input refusal for codepoints that make a WYSIWYS rendering misrepresent the signed action to a human approver. This is NOT the EP-DISPLAY-ATTESTATION-v1 wire format: no artifact is produced, an action carrying these codepoints is refused before any receipt is minted. Refusal rather than in-renderer neutralization keeps the frozen EP-WYSIWYS-RENDER-v1 profile and every existing display_hash byte-identical.
residual_risk: Homoglyph substitution (Cyrillic a for Latin a) is NOT refused here: it has legitimate uses and no bright-line test, so it remains an operational and directory-level control. This guard covers only codepoints with no legitimate reading inside a rendered identifier: bidi overrides, zero-width/BOM, and C0/C1 controls.

must_reject.title: Bidirectional override inside a rendered action field spoofs the approver's display
must_reject.attack: target_resource_id is 'acct-9931' followed by U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE and then 'live'. The renderer passed the codepoint through, so the approver read 'acct-9931evil' while the signed bytes said otherwise. action_hash and display_hash BOTH cover the hostile bytes, so the display attestation verifies and the rendering is faithful to the signed action: the deception is purely visual, aimed at the human at the moment of decision.

must_reject.title: Zero-width and C0/C1 control characters in rendered action fields
must_reject.attack: actor_id or policy_id carries U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE, a C0 control (U+0000) or a C1 control (U+0085). These hide or fuse content in the rendering without changing what the signature covers.

must_reject.title: Hostile codepoint nested inside a structured rendered field, including an object key
must_reject.attack: risk_flags array members and rollout_metadata values are rendered via the canonical serializer, and object KEYS render alongside values. A hostile codepoint in either is refused, so nesting is not an escape hatch.

must_accept.title: Arabic and Hebrew content renders normally; the script is not the attack
must_accept.shape: target_resource_id and actor_id carry ordinary Arabic and Hebrew text with no override codepoints. The guard classifies override/zero-width/control codepoints, never scripts. Negative control proving the refusal is not a blanket non-ASCII ban.

must_accept.title: Tab, newline and carriage return are not control-character attacks
must_accept.shape: policy_id contains tab and newline. These are everyday whitespace, explicitly excluded from the C0 refusal set, and must keep passing.

must_accept.title: Hostile bytes in a field the renderer never displays are ignored
must_accept.shape: A non-rendered field carries U+202E. It cannot deceive an approver because it is never displayed, so refusing it would reject legitimate payloads for no security gain. The guard is scoped to what a human actually sees.
